claims.text: A facile spray-coating process can deposit a thin 2D (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 HEA film on component surfaces.
A single (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 coating will reduce both friction and wear relative to untreated HEA surfaces across a wide service-temperature range.
The untreated baseline consists of HEA surfaces with conventional microstructures used in self-lubricating components.
The (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 coating provides low friction and wear under high contact pressure.
The coating remains effective from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures.
The coating retains its phase stability and tribocatalytic activity throughout the proposed temperature range.
The layered 2D structure of (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 facilitates shear-induced energy dissipation at sliding interfaces.
The (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 HEA activates tribocatalytic activity at the sliding interface under high contact pressure.
Sliding causes shear-induced transformations in the coating that trigger its tribocatalytic activity.
Tribocatalytic activity forms lubricious phases in situ.
The coating's self-adaptive behavior minimizes crack propagation and film delamination.
Shear-induced energy dissipation and tribocatalytic activity contribute to the coating's low-friction, long-lived lubrication.
The coated system can attain an average coefficient of friction of approximately 0.076 under high contact pressure at ambient conditions.
The coated system can attain a wear rate on the order of 10^-9 mm3/(N·m) under high contact pressure at ambient conditions.
Untreated HEA components have higher friction and wear than coated components under otherwise similar conditions.
The approximately 0.076 friction coefficient and 10^-9 mm3/(N·m) wear rate will persist as operating temperature varies.
Performance may be compromised when service temperature exceeds the thermal-stability limit of the 2D film.
Extreme thermal cycling may degrade the coating.
Excellent tribological performance has been demonstrated under ambient conditions.
